questions.stem: DIRECT TAXES are levied on income/wealth and paid directly by the taxpayer to the government. Which of the following is a DIRECT tax?

options.option_text: GST
Customs duty
Income Tax
Service Tax

questions.explanation: TAXES in India — two types: (1) DIRECT TAXES (paid by the person/entity on whom they are levied; incidence + impact on same person): INCOME TAX (individuals, HUFs), CORPORATE TAX (companies), CAPITAL GAINS TAX (property/shares), SECURITIES TRANSACTION TAX (STT), MINIMUM ALTERNATE TAX (MAT — on companies with low tax due to deductions), DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION TAX (DDT — abolished 2020), WEALTH TAX (abolished 2015 in favour of surcharge). GIFT TAX (abolished 1998, reintroduced indirectly in IT Act). ESTATE DUTY (abolished 1985). (2) INDIRECT TAXES (shifted from seller to buyer via price; incidence on one, impact on another): GST (since 2017 — subsumed Excise, Service Tax, VAT, etc.), CUSTOMS DUTY (on imports/exports), EXCISE (now only on petroleum products + alcohol), STAMP DUTY. CENTRAL BOARD OF DIRECT TAXES (CBDT) — Direct taxes; CENTRAL BOARD OF INDIRECT TAXES & CUSTOMS (CBIC) — Indirect. Both under Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue). Direct taxes are PROGRESSIVE (higher income → higher rate); indirect are REGRESSIVE (flat rate burdens poor more). + Corporate Tax, Capital Gains, Wealth Tax discontinued.
questions.subject: Economics

_fixes.was: Income Tax (+ Corporate Tax, Capital Gains, Wealth Tax discontinued)

questions.stem: The GST COUNCIL — the supreme decision-making body for GST — is headed by:

options.option_text: The Prime Minister
The Union Finance Minister
The President of India
The Attorney General

questions.explanation: GST COUNCIL — constitutional body under ARTICLE 279-A (inserted by 101st Amendment 2016). Composition: UNION FINANCE MINISTER (chairperson); Union MoS Finance (member); Finance Minister of EACH STATE (members — picked by state). VOTING: decisions need 3/4 majority. CENTRE HAS 1/3 weight; STATES HAVE 2/3 weight (equally divided). Has been the primary forum for GST rate changes, exemptions, procedural tweaks. As of 2024, 50+ council meetings held. Effective 1 JULY 2017 — GST was India's biggest tax reform. Replaced ~17 indirect taxes. FOUR SLABS: 0% (essentials — unbranded food, services for underprivileged), 5% (household items), 12% (processed food, mobile phones), 18% (most services + goods — standard rate), 28% (luxury + sin goods). ADDITIONAL CESS on some 28% items (luxury cars, tobacco, aerated drinks). EXCLUDED: alcohol (state-controlled), 5 petroleum products, electricity duty, stamp duty.

questions.stem: GST in India has FOUR components depending on nature of supply. Which TAX is levied on INTER-STATE supplies?

options.option_text: CGST (Central GST)
IGST (Integrated GST)
SGST (State GST)
UTGST (Union Territory GST)

questions.explanation: GST components: (1) CGST (Central GST) — on INTRA-state supplies; goes to CENTRE. (2) SGST (State GST) — on intra-state supplies; goes to STATE where consumed. CGST + SGST rate = GST rate (e.g., 18% GST = 9% CGST + 9% SGST). (3) UTGST (Union Territory GST) — same as SGST but for UTs without legislature (Chandigarh, A&N Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra & Nagar Haveli & Daman & Diu, Ladakh). Delhi, Puducherry, J&K have legislatures → use SGST. (4) IGST (Integrated GST) — on INTER-STATE supplies (goods moving between states) + IMPORTS; collected by CENTRE, then split between Centre + destination state. Rate = full GST rate (18% = 18% IGST, no split at collection). ORIGIN-BASED vs DESTINATION-BASED: GST is DESTINATION-BASED — tax goes where goods/services are consumed. This was a big shift from earlier origin-based taxes. REVERSE CHARGE MECHANISM (RCM): for specific goods/services, recipient pays GST instead of supplier.

questions.stem: The current (FY 2024-25) income tax slab under the NEW REGIME (default since 2023) for an individual, with the basic exemption limit at:

options.option_text: ₹2.5 lakh
₹3 lakh
₹5 lakh
₹10 lakh

questions.explanation: INCOME TAX in India — TWO REGIMES (since Budget 2020, further tweaked 2023/24): (A) OLD REGIME — higher slab rates but allows deductions (80C, 80D, HRA, LTA, home loan interest etc.). (B) NEW REGIME — lower rates + wider slabs, BUT NO most deductions (just standard deduction). DEFAULT switched to NEW REGIME from FY 2023-24. NEW REGIME SLABS (FY 2024-25, for individuals below 60): (1) ₹0 – ₹3 L = NIL; (2) ₹3-7 L = 5%; (3) ₹7-10 L = 10%; (4) ₹10-12 L = 15%; (5) ₹12-15 L = 20%; (6) > ₹15 L = 30%. REBATE u/s 87A: income up to ₹7 lakh → NO TAX under new regime (rebate up to ₹25k). STANDARD DEDUCTION ₹75k (raised from 50k in Budget 2024). SURCHARGE on income > ₹50L (10% → 37% progressive, but capped at 25% under new regime). CESS 4% (health + education). CORPORATE TAX RATES: domestic 22% (concessional, if foregoing exemptions) + 15% for new manufacturing companies (sunset). RATES CHANGE EVERY BUDGET — HIGH STALENESS. new regime FY 2024-25; rebate u/s 87A means no tax up to ₹7 lakh.

questions.stem: Which state in India was the FIRST to agree to implement GST, passing its resolution on 16 May 2017 (before 1 July rollout)?

options.option_text: Gujarat
Telangana
Tamil Nadu
Maharashtra

questions.explanation: TELANGANA — FIRST STATE to pass its GST Bill on 16 May 2017 (before the national 1 July 2017 rollout). Followed closely by Bihar, Rajasthan, Gujarat, etc. GST was enabled by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 (September 2016) — longest-debated amendment, introduced as 115th Amendment Bill in 2011 by UPA, finally passed in 2016. Four GST Acts passed by Parliament (April 2017): CGST Act, IGST Act, UTGST Act, GST (Compensation to States) Act. GST implementation in India: July 2017 (18 years after Atal Bihari Vajpayee first proposed it in 2000, Kelkar Task Force endorsed in 2003). Modelled loosely on Canadian + French VAT systems. GST replaced: Central Excise, Service Tax, VAT, Entertainment Tax, Entry Tax, CST, Purchase Tax, Luxury Tax, Octroi, Advertising Tax, etc. GST Compensation Cess — for 5 years (extended) to compensate states for any revenue loss during transition. GST COUNCIL meets regularly to rationalise rates, handle issues. first, 16 May 2017.

questions.stem: Which Constitutional Amendment empowered the Union to tax incomes?

options.option_text: Via original Constitution 1950
101st Amendment (GST)
82nd Amendment
42nd Amendment

questions.explanation: Under the original INDIAN CONSTITUTION 1950, taxation powers are DIVIDED between Centre + States via the 7TH SCHEDULE (three lists): UNION LIST (Entry 82-92B for Union taxes): INCOME TAX (except agricultural income — state), CORPORATION TAX, CUSTOMS, EXCISE (historical — now mostly GST), SERVICE TAX (historical — now GST), wealth tax (abolished), estate duty (abolished). STATE LIST (Entries 45-63): AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX, LAND REVENUE, STAMP DUTY (non-documents), EXCISE on ALCOHOL, TAXES ON VEHICLES, STATE EXCISE, ENTRY TAXES (now in GST), PROFESSIONAL TAX (capped at ₹2500/year via Art 276). CONCURRENT LIST: trade + commerce, stamp duty on certain documents. Fiscal federalism: FINANCE COMMISSION (Art 280) — every 5 years divides tax revenues between Centre-States. 15th FC period 2021-26 (chairman NK Singh) gave states 41% of divisible tax pool (down from 42% under 14th FC). 101st Amendment (2016) added Article 246-A overriding both Union + State lists to enable GST. IMPORTANT: INCOME from agriculture STILL tax-free at Centre but taxable by States — loophole for high-income farmers (though rarely enforced by states). 7th Schedule — Union List.
questions.subject: Economics

_fixes.was: Via original Constitution 1950 (7th Schedule — Union List)

questions.stem: The THRESHOLD for GST registration for businesses dealing in GOODS is:

options.option_text: ₹5 lakh annual turnover
₹40 lakh annual turnover (₹20 lakh for Special Category States); ₹20 lakh for services
₹1 crore
No threshold — all must register

questions.explanation: GST Registration Thresholds (FY 2024-25): GOODS — ₹40 lakh annual turnover (normal states); ₹20 lakh (Special Category States: Arunachal, Assam, J&K, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Himachal, Uttarakhand). SERVICES — ₹20 lakh (normal); ₹10 lakh (Special Category). Below these, GST registration is OPTIONAL (businesses can still register voluntarily to claim input tax credit). MANDATORY registration REGARDLESS of turnover for: inter-state suppliers, e-commerce operators + sellers, casual taxable persons, reverse charge liable, those supplying through e-commerce, non-resident taxable persons. COMPOSITION SCHEME: small businesses up to ₹1.5 crore can opt for fixed low rates — 1% (manufacturers/traders), 5% (restaurants), 6% (services) — but can't claim ITC + can't sell inter-state. GST FILING: monthly/quarterly returns — GSTR-1 (outward), GSTR-3B (summary), GSTR-9 (annual). GSTN = Goods and Services Tax Network — technology backbone (51% private, originally; now fully govt after May 2018 restructuring).

questions.stem: GST in India is described as a 'destination-based consumption tax.' What does this specifically mean in terms of tax revenue allocation?

options.option_text: Revenue accrues to the state where the manufacturing unit is located
Revenue accrues to the state where goods or services are finally consumed
Revenue goes to Central Government and is redistributed via Finance Commission
Revenue accrues to the state where the supplier's head office is registered

questions.explanation: Under destination-based taxation, GST revenue belongs to the consuming state, not the producing one. This replaced the origin-based CST/VAT framework and directly benefits consumption-heavy states. Option A describes the old origin-based system that GST was specifically designed to replace.

questions.stem: Among the following, which commodity is placed in the HIGHEST GST slab of 28% in India?

options.option_text: Packaged food items sold under registered brand names (5–12% slab)
Household fans, coolers, and similar domestic appliances (18% slab)
Mobile phones and consumer electronics after their 2020 revision (18% slab)
Cement used in construction and infrastructure development (28% slab)

questions.explanation: Cement attracts 28% GST despite being a critical infrastructure input — a frequently tested anomaly. Mobile phones were moved to 18% in 2020. Fans attract 18%. Branded packaged food ranges 5–12%. Candidates often confuse cement with lower-rate construction inputs like steel (18%), making D the most commonly missed option.

questions.stem: Under GST law, 'ZERO-RATED SUPPLY' and 'NIL-RATED SUPPLY' are not the same. Which statement CORRECTLY distinguishes them?

options.option_text: Both terms are fully interchangeable; both describe supplies entirely free from GST
Nil-rated covers exports and SEZ supplies; zero-rated covers all domestically exempt goods
Zero-rated (exports/SEZ) allows ITC refund; nil-rated domestic goods deny ITC claims
Zero-rated means the output tax rate is 0%; nil-rated means no invoice is required

questions.explanation: Section 16 of the IGST Act defines zero-rated supply as exports and SEZ supplies — crucially, the supplier can claim a refund of input tax credit even though no output tax is charged. Nil-rated domestic supplies (fresh vegetables, salt) attract 0% GST but the supplier CANNOT reclaim ITC on inputs. Option B reverses the definitions — a classic examiner trap exploiting candidates who confuse the two.

questions.stem: A manufacturer of PAN MASALA with annual turnover of ₹80 lakh wants to reduce compliance burden by opting for the GST Composition Scheme. Is this permissible?

options.option_text: Yes, any manufacturer below the ₹1.5 crore turnover threshold can freely opt in
Yes, but the manufacturer must obtain prior approval from the GST Council first
No, manufacturers of pan masala, tobacco, and ice cream are specifically excluded
No, because the Composition Scheme is available only to traders, not to manufacturers

questions.explanation: Section 10 of the CGST Act explicitly bars manufacturers of pan masala, tobacco products, and ice cream from the Composition Scheme regardless of their turnover — a PYQ-frequent fact. Option D is a common distractor: manufacturers of other goods CAN opt in up to ₹1.5 crore. Only these three categories carry an absolute product-based exclusion, not a general manufacturing bar.

questions.stem: A Delhi-based architect provides design services for a building under construction in Goa. The client is registered in Maharashtra. Under GST, the PLACE OF SUPPLY of this service will be:

options.option_text: Delhi, because the architect is registered as a GST taxpayer in Delhi state
Goa, as the immovable property is located in Goa per Section 12(3) of IGST Act
Maharashtra, being the state where the service recipient is registered or domiciled
The state where the agreement for architectural services was formally executed

questions.explanation: Section 12(3) of the IGST Act mandates that the place of supply for services related to immovable property — including architecture, interior design, and civil construction — is the location of the property itself. Goa being the property's location makes this an inter-state supply attracting IGST. Options A and C reflect the most common misapplication of the general rule (supplier's or recipient's location) which applies only when no specific rule exists.

questions.stem: Section 17(5) of the CGST Act creates a 'BLOCKED CREDITS' list — Input Tax Credit that cannot be claimed. Which of the following correctly identifies a blocked credit?

options.option_text: GST paid on raw materials used to manufacture a taxable output product
GST paid on outdoor catering services arranged for the company's employees
GST paid on goods exported under a valid Letter of Undertaking (LUT)
GST paid on capital machinery used exclusively in providing taxable services

questions.explanation: Section 17(5)(b) of the CGST Act specifically blocks ITC on food and beverages, outdoor catering, health services, and similar personal consumption items — even when provided at the workplace for employees. Options A (raw materials for taxable output), C (export under LUT as zero-rated supply), and D (capital equipment for taxable services) all qualify for ITC and are placed as tempting distractors testing whether the candidate has memorised the blocked list versus the general eligibility rule.

questions.stem: The MINIMUM ALTERNATE TAX (MAT) under Section 115JB of the Income Tax Act was reduced by the Taxation Laws Ordinance, 2019. What is the revised MAT rate currently applicable?

options.option_text: 10% of book profit, rationalised for domestic companies post-2022 reforms
15% of book profit, reduced from 18.5% by the Taxation Laws Ordinance, 2019
18.5% of book profit, the original rate applicable since MAT was first introduced
20% of book profit, uniformly applicable to all domestic companies in India

questions.explanation: The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance 2019 reduced MAT from 18.5% to 15% of book profit (plus applicable surcharge and cess) — announced simultaneously with the cut in base corporate tax rates to 22%. Option C (18.5%) is the sharpest distractor: it was the long-standing rate for over a decade and many candidates have outdated notes. MAT is calculated on book profit under the Companies Act, not on taxable income, which is its defining distinction from regular income tax.
